missionPremise: P-109 WDLL: export_instrument exists, has a trigger, and its gating precondition (HAUSKA_MCP_BASE_URL / HAUSKA_MCP_SERVICE_KEY) is never supplied on the serving revision. Starved, which reports as success. Item 1 orders the measurement BEFORE any configuration.
completionPredicate: Either export_instrument performs a real export end to end, or it is established that the upstream does not exist and the tool stops being advertised as available; plus a named control (or a declared absence) keeping catalog and runtime in agreement, every check shown failing on a deliberate violation.
scopeBasis: The card forbids building an export engine, forbids changing the Studio gate (P-101 owns it, open PR #586), and forbids touching artifacts/smartsite-mcp/src/tools.ts beyond the minimum item 3 requires because open PRs hold it.

item1_measurement.verdict: NEITHER FORK AS WRITTEN. Third state: the upstream CAPABILITY is present and live, a CREDENTIAL is present and paid-entitled, and the CLIENT CONTRACT the smartsite-mcp proxy is coded against has never existed in any server.

The endpoint the smartsite-mcp proxy calls, POST {HAUSKA_MCP_BASE_URL}/tools/export_instrument, exists.
corroboration: git grep for express route registrations on hauska-mcp-server origin/main src lists NO /tools/* route; the server speaks MCP JSON-RPC on POST /mcp
git grep -n export_instrument origin/main (hauska-mcp-server) returns NOTHING

git grep -n 'tools/export_instrument' origin/main (legacy-design-tools) returns exactly two hits: src/export-instrument.ts:86 (the client) and tests/tools.test.ts:2059 (a mock of it). The path exists only in the caller and in a fixture that mocks the caller.

findings.claim: A secret named PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL is the base URL to configure.
findings.result: It is a POSTGRES DSN (postgresql://neondb_owner:<redacted>@ep-lucky-truth-apodo8hr...neon.tech/hauska_mcp), not an HTTP base URL. STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL likewise. An agent taking the configure-durably branch and reaching for the obviously-named secret would have set HAUSKA_MCP_BASE_URL to a database connection string. Value redacted deliberately; it is a live credential.

item1_measurement.consequence: Setting HAUSKA_MCP_BASE_URL and HAUSKA_MCP_SERVICE_KEY on the serving revision would NOT make export_instrument work. It would move the failure from an honest not-configured refusal to a 404 HTML body returned as isError, on a tool that then reports itself as configured. That is strictly worse: a starved control becomes a broken one wearing a working one's clothes. Item 2 is therefore NOT taken.

designDecision.chosen: Item 3 branch, in the form the codebase already has for this exact situation: flip export_instrument to readiness blocked in artifacts/smartsite-mcp/src/constants.ts with a blockedReason naming P-109, and rewrite its description so it stops claiming a working proxy.
whyThisForm: SMARTSITE_MCP_TOOLS in src/constants.ts is the SINGLE source for both surfaces: renderLlmsTxt (src/health.ts:63) renders the not-ready suffix when readiness === blocked, and registerTools (src/tools.ts:508) iterates the same array and short-circuits a blocked tool to notReadyMessage before any other branch. One edit moves the catalog and the runtime together.
Three tools already use this exact form: request_records, check_request, ask_the_map. ask_the_map's blockedReason is literally that its path is unwired - the same class of defect.
It requires ZERO edits to artifacts/smartsite-mcp/src/tools.ts, which the card ring-fences.

Blocking BEFORE the Studio gate is the more honest order. Today a free caller is told upgrade_required/studio_report for a capability no tier can obtain: tools.test.ts already asserts 'studio session passes studio gate but export remains not_ready'. Selling an upgrade for a capability that does not exist is the defect P-104's lane was spent on.

rejectedAlternatives.option: Delete the export_instrument entry from SMARTSITE_MCP_TOOLS entirely (strongest form of stop-advertising: it disappears from tools/list too).
rejectedAlternatives.rejected: SmartsiteToolName is derived from that array, so removing the name makes the export_instrument case labels in inputSchemaFor and in the registerTools switch non-overlapping-type comparisons. tsc forces edits to src/tools.ts, which two open PRs hold and the card forbids beyond a catalog line. Routed to the planner as the stronger follow-up, not taken here.
Measured: the target endpoint 404s. Configuring produces a false configured state. Fail-closed says refuse rather than emit an unverified value.

rejectedAlternatives.option: Rewire executeExportInstrument to speak MCP JSON-RPC to refresh_/download_parcel_*_export.
rejectedAlternatives.rejected: That is a build, not a config fix, and it is blocked on rulings this lane cannot make: there is no upstream brief export kind; the two-hop refresh-then-download shape does not match the one-shot client; the upstream tools are public-paid and SDK-metered per refresh while smartsite-mcp callers already pay Stripe, so metering would double-charge without a ruling. Routed as a new plan row.

item4_controlDesign.todayTheAnswerIsNothing: No executor, no trigger, and nothing fails when the declared catalog and the runtime disagree. readiness is hand-declared in constants.ts; the refusal that contradicts it is hardcoded in tools.ts. export_instrument sat readiness live while its handler always refused, and no check anywhere could fire.

proposed.trigger: the smartsite-mcp test job in CI on every PR and push
proposed.failsWhen: a tool declared readiness live in SMARTSITE_MCP_TOOLS has a hardcoded notReadyMessage refusal naming that tool in src/tools.ts
proposed.bypassedBy: a tool that always refuses for some OTHER reason (an upstream that always 500s, a permanently-false feature flag); anything not run through CI; a refusal written in a file other than tools.ts
proposed.honestLimit: This is an INTERNAL CONSISTENCY check, not a meaning-shaped one. Both sides are authored in one package by one party, so one party acting alone can satisfy both. It catches declaration drift, which is exactly the P-109 defect, and it does NOT catch a tool that is declared live and is broken upstream. The meaning-shaped version needs a second derivation - a probe of the DEPLOYED server asserting no live-declared tool returns status not_ready - and that is blocked on CI holding a WorkOS OAuth session. Declared unbuilt, not implied.

constraintsHonored: No git add / commit / push / PR / merge / deploy in any repo.
Every command exit-bounded; no watch, tail, follow, or server.
Traffic read as JSON by field name, never the positional value(...) formatter.
Env read off the SERVING REVISION (smartsite-mcp-00085-nuj), never the service template.
No credential created or rotated. HAUSKA_MCP_KEY read to probe, never printed, never written to an artifact.
